_meta.policy: Rates are legal rules, not personalized liabilities. Blank personal amounts remain unverified.

positions.position: A remittance of already-taxed principal is not itself one of the nine IIT income categories. Underlying income/gains may still be taxable; do not treat a bank transfer as a taxable event by default.

positions.topic: PRC tax residence vs FX classification
positions.position: IIT residence (domicile / 183 days) and bank FX classification (domestic vs overseas individual) are different tests. A U.S. citizen may be an overseas individual for FX but still a PRC tax resident, or vice versa.

positions.topic: Salary, services, rent, royalties and other income
positions.position: Tax depends on the income category and residence. Comprehensive income has progressive rates; business income 5%-35%; interest/dividends/property lease/property transfer/incidental income generally 20% proportional. Do not apply one flat rate to the whole bank balance.

Generally 20% of transfer income minus original value and reasonable expenses with valid documents. If original value cannot be verified, tax authorities may assess 1%-3% of transfer income under the 2006 notice. Five-year sole-family-home exemption may apply. Local implementation and later policies must be checked.
positions.rate: 20% of gain; assessed alternative 1%-3% of income where applicable

positions.topic: FIE dividends to foreign individuals from 2026-09-01
positions.position: MOF/STA 2026 No. 27 repeals the old exemption: FIE dividends to foreign individuals are taxed as interest/dividend income at 20%, with withholding by the FIE. Treaty relief may reduce source tax if conditions are met.

positions.topic: FIE dividends to nonresident corporate shareholders
positions.position: Specified nonresident-enterprise China-source income is subject to a reduced 10% EIT rate under Implementation Regulations Art. 91, with withholding mechanics. Treaty beneficial-owner/residence analysis is separate.
positions.rate: 10% statutory reduced rate; treaty may differ

positions.position: For covered outbound service-trade payments, tax filing is required before the first payment exceeding USD50k under the same contract. Filing is not itself a tax and does not replace withholding/IIT/EIT/VAT analysis.
A U.S. citizen is generally taxed on worldwide income. China-source salary, rent, dividends, gains and FX gains may need U.S. reporting even if the money never leaves China.

Credit is limited to qualifying foreign income taxes and U.S. tax on foreign-source income; treaty-reduced tax only qualifies. No credit for tax on FEIE-excluded income. It is not an automatic full offset.

IRC §988 generally treats FX gain/loss as ordinary, but personal transactions are excluded. For a personal disposition of nonfunctional currency, gain is not recognized unless it exceeds USD200; if it exceeds USD200, the exclusion does not apply to the transaction. IRS Pub. 525 says report a personal FX gain over USD200 as a capital gain. Basis, holding period and personal-vs-investment character are fact-dependent.
positions.rate: USD200 transaction threshold; not a USD200 deduction

positions.position: U.S. persons with aggregate foreign financial accounts exceeding USD10k at any time must file FinCEN Form 114. It is separate from the tax return. Penalties are fact-dependent; nonwillful maximum is per report under Bittner, adjusted for inflation.

Specified individuals must check separate thresholds: U.S. residents unmarried/MFS >50k year-end or >75k anytime; joint >100k/>150k. Abroad unmarried/MFS >200k/>300k; joint >400k/>600k. Form 8938 does not replace FBAR.

U.S. persons receiving >USD100k aggregate from a nonresident alien/foreign estate generally report on Form 3520; related-party aggregation applies. 2026 purported-gift threshold from foreign corporations/partnerships is USD20,573. Covered-expatriate gifts/bequests may trigger §2801 tax.
Applies from 2026-01-01 to specified remittances sent from the United States funded by cash/money order/cashier's check or similar physical instrument. It is not a China-to-U.S. transfer cost.

The U.S.-China treaty preserves U.S. taxation of its citizens subject to listed exceptions. Treaty dividend/interest caps require residence/beneficial ownership and do not erase U.S. reporting or domestic tax.
PRC IIT law requires tax clearance before cancelling household registration when emigrating. SAFE property-transfer guides require tax certificates unless exempt.
